story.originalTitle: 'Not many sports teams have done it' - Wolff 'proud' of Mercedes turnaround
story.summaryEn: Mercedes clinched the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship with three races to spare at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, the team's ninth constructors' title. Toto Wolff said he is "proud" of Mercedes' turnaround and feels very few sports teams have bounced back so quickly.
detailZh: 托托·沃尔夫在圣保罗大奖赛锁定2026赛季F1车队总冠军后，为梅赛德斯的逆转感到“自豪”。
梅赛德斯在2026赛季还剩三站时赢得队史第九个F1车队总冠军；梅赛德斯曾在2014至2021年间连续八次夺冠，此后经历了一段低谷期，托托·沃尔夫对银箭车队的反弹方式尤为自豪。
梅赛德斯在锁定第九个车队总冠军后于领奖台庆祝。
托托·沃尔夫表示，他为梅赛德斯逆转夺得2026赛季F1车队总冠军感到“自豪”，并认为很少有体育队伍能这么快完成反弹。
梅赛德斯在周日的圣保罗大奖赛上赢得了他们的第九个车队总冠军，距离他们上一次夺冠已经过去五年，当时那是他们连续第八个车队冠军。
2022年的规则变更终结了梅赛德斯的统治地位，他们难以驾驭所谓的“地面效应”赛车，但他们赢得了2026年新规赛车的首个赛季，并且本月早些时候还凭借基米·安东内利锁定了车手总冠军。

沃尔夫表示：“问题是，当你身处这些艰难时刻——就像我们每个人在生活中有时也会经历的那样——坚持下去并不容易。”
“事后回想起来，你会说：‘我们需要这些艰难时刻，才能作为个人成长，或者作为组织成长。’但当你身处低谷时，很难有这种感觉。
“我觉得过去这四年非常艰难，先是做错了，然后多少明白为什么错了，接着又意识到不，我们其实没搞懂。那段时间有点反反复复。
“但十年或二十年后我们会回望。当你看看统计数据，那四年里我们并不是彻底的输家，因为我们拿了第二、（第二）、第三、第四（在年度积分榜上），我们赢过分站，赢过很多分站。所以单看数字，根本没那么糟，但感觉并不好。”
托托·沃尔夫对梅赛德斯在巴西赢得车队总冠军作出回应
正如沃尔夫所指出的，梅赛德斯在2022年至2025年间仍然赢下了比赛，乔治·拉塞尔和刘易斯·汉密尔顿两人合计赢得七场大奖赛。
“车队的韧性，以及那些在艰难时期团结在一起的人们，我认为是一个因素，”沃尔夫继续说道。
“锁定这两个冠军的感觉真的很好。没有多少体育团队能在连续夺冠之后经历一段困难时期、然后再度回归并做到这一点，所以我非常自豪我们属于在所有体育项目中做到这一点的极少数团队之一。”
2026年圣保罗大奖赛精彩集锦
梅赛德斯在车队总冠军数量上追平威廉姆斯，同为九次夺冠——在F1历史上，只有迈凯伦（10次）和法拉利（16次）比他们更多。
沃尔夫表示，他的自豪感源于梅赛德斯位于英国布拉克利和布里克斯沃思的工厂所付出的辛勤努力，这些努力让车队在本赛季平均而言打造出了最好的赛车。
“有时候，车手们或者我自己，会因为出现在电视镜头前而备受关注，但有太多人参与其中，”他告诉天空体育F1频道。
“我总是说，明星车手并不是只有两位，而是有2500位明星，他们都在出色地完成工作，我们所有人共同为这样一个锦标赛贡献力量。”
基米·安东内利回应梅赛德斯夺得第九个世界车队冠军
在巴西，梅赛德斯两位车手都未能登上领奖台，兰多·诺里斯在混合条件下占据统治地位，而安东内利和拉塞尔都发生了打转。
拉塞尔获得第四名，紧随其后的是安东内利，他表示梅赛德斯的每个人都“配得上”今年的成功。
这位意大利车手告诉天空体育F1：“他们这一年做得非常出色，这是一群了不起的人，每天都在全力以赴，为我们争取胜利和冠军提供最好的机会。”
“今年他们干得非常棒，正因如此他们配得上这个冠军，我们会一起享受这一刻。”
乔治·拉塞尔表示，在两辆赛车分别以第四和第五名完赛后，梅赛德斯本希望能以更风光的方式赢得车队总冠军。
拉塞尔补充道：“我们完成了来这里的目标，赢得了车队总冠军。我们本希望能更有风采一些，但对车队每个人来说这都是了不起的成就。”
“我们经历了艰难的四年，整个组织付出了巨大努力，才让我们回到这个位置。2022年我加入梅赛德斯时，我们曾希望自己能经常为冠军而战，所以走过这段旅程、如今重返巅峰，是我们所有人都应该无比自豪的事情。”

detailEn: Toto Wolff 'proud' of Mercedes turnaround after winning F1 2026 Constructors' Championship at Sao Paulo Grand Prix

Mercedes won their ninth F1 Constructors' Championship with three races to spare of the 2026 season; Mercedes won eight in a row between 2014 and 2021 before a fallow period and Toto Wolff is particularly proud of how the Silver Arrows bounced back
Mercedes party on the podium after sealing their ninth Constructors' Championship title
Toto Wolff says he's "proud" of Mercedes' turnaround to win the 2026 Formula 1 Constructors' Championship and feels very few sports teams have bounced back so quickly.
Mercedes won their ninth constructors' title on Sunday at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, five years after their last championship, which was their eighth in a row at the time.

Regulation changes in 2022 ended Mercedes' dominance as they struggled to get on top of the so-called ground effect cars, but they have won the first season of the new 2026 cars, and also wrapped up the Drivers' Championship earlier this month with Kimi Antonelli.

"The thing is when you are in these difficult moments, like we all are sometimes in our lives, it's not that easy to keep going," said Wolff.
"Looking back in retrospect, you're saying, 'we needed these tough moments in order to grow as people or to grow as an organisation'. But when you're down, that is quite difficult to feel.
"I think those last four years were very difficult between getting it wrong, then kind of understanding why it was wrong and then realising no we didn't understand. That was a bit back and forth.

"But we will be looking back in 10 or 20 years. When you look at the statistics, it wasn't that we were complete losers over those four years, because we finished second, (second), third, fourth [in the championship], we won races, won many races. So it wasn't that bad at all when you look at the sheer numbers, but it felt not good."
Toto Wolff reacts to Mercedes winning the Constructors' Championship in Brazil
As Wolff points out, Mercedes still won races between 2022 and 2025, with George Russell and Lewis Hamilton winning seven Grands Prix between them.
"The resilience of the team, the people that held together in those tough times, is a factor, I think," continued Wolff.

"It feels really good sealing those two titles. Not many sports teams have done that after consecutive run of championships, then a difficult spell and then coming back, so I'm really proud that we are part of this very small group of teams that have done that in all sports."
Highlights from the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix
Mercedes move level with Williams on nine constructors' titles - only McLaren (10) and Ferrari (16) have more in Formula 1 history.
Wolff says his pride comes from the hard work in Mercedes' UK factories in Brackley and Brixworth to produce the best car, on average, this season.
"Sometimes the drivers, or myself, we are so visible because we are in in front of the TV cameras, but there's so many people that are part of this," he told Sky Sports F1.
"I always say there are not two superstars, the drivers, but there are 2,500 superstars, all of them delivering a great job, being all of us contributing to such a championship."
Kimi Antonelli reacts to Mercedes claiming their ninth world constructors championship
Mercedes were unable to finish with either of their drivers on the podium in Brazil as Lando Norris dominated in mixed conditions, while Antonelli and Russell both spun.
Russell finished in fourth, just ahead of Antonelli who says everyone at Mercedes "deserves" this year's success.

"They have done an incredible year and it's an amazing group of people, who push every day to do their best and give us the best opportunity to fight for wins and championships," the Italian told Sky Sports F1.
"This year they have done an incredible job and that's why they deserve this championship and we will enjoy it together."
George Russell says Mercedes would've liked to win the Constructors' Championship title in style after both cars finished fourth and fifth respectively

Russell added: "We achieved what we came here to do and won the Constructors' Championship. We would have liked to have done it in a bit more style, but it's an incredible achievement for everyone in the team.

"We've had four difficult years and the whole organisation put so much work into getting us back into this position. When I joined Mercedes in 2022, we hoped we'd be fighting for championships regularly, so to have gone through that journey and now get back to the top is something we should all be incredibly proud of."

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.

汉密尔顿在整个练习赛中都很不高兴，并在他的最后一圈飞驰后表示他的“赛车无法转向”，这使他排在第九位，位于小红牛车队的Arvid Lindblad和劳森之间。

detailEn: Qatar GP: Kimi Antonelli fastest in final practice from George Russell as Mercedes domination continues ahead of qualifying

Kimi Antonelli led George Russell in another Mercedes one-two in final practice at the Lusail International Circuit; watch Qualifying at 6pm later on Saturday and the Qatar Grand Prix at 4pm on Sunday, live on Sky Sports F1

George Russell says Lewis Hamilton is an equally 'ruthless competitor' to Max Verstappen but that his former team-mate has 'incredible values, grace and dignity'. Watch the full interview during Sky Sports F1's live Qatar GP coverage on Sunday
Kimi Antonelli outpaced Mercedes team-mate George Russell in final practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as the Silver Arrows continued to dominate.

Antonelli, who topped both of Friday's practice sessions, outpaced Russell by 0.249s and it looks highly likely a Mercedes driver will be on pole position after qualifying, which takes place later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Mercedes appear to have a half-second advantage over the rest field as Max Verstappen was 0.510s adrift of Antonelli and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was 0.687s behind.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.
"Mercedes are almost in a class of their own, so it's worth the rest looking at the gap to Verstappen [in third]," said Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins.

Ferrari had a difficult Friday after a spin for Charles Leclerc and an engine issue for Lewis Hamilton, but Leclerc fared better in final practice in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton was unhappy throughout the session and stated his "car won't turn" after his final flying lap which put him in ninth, in between Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson.
